info.title: wan/wan2.6-i2v
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "wan/wan2.6-i2v", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description:
The Wan / HappyHorse video-generation fields, shared by the v1 `POST /proxy/wan/api/v1/services/aigc/video-generation/video-synthesis` request body and the Comfy Router input schema. This is a shared validation floor, not the complete contract of each provider model. Image-to-video, reference-to-video and editing models need model-specific reference inputs; supported resolutions and duration ranges also vary by model. The proxy additionally requires parameters with a recognized size or resolution for billing. Schema acceptance alone does not imply provider acceptance.
`required` here is the ROUTER-SAFE floor: `model` is absent from it because Router writes the path's model into the body after routervalidate.Guard has already validated the caller's bytes. The v1 wrapper `WanVideoGenerationRequest` re-adds it.

input.description: Enter basic information, such as prompt words, etc.

audio_url.description: Audio file download URL. Supported formats: mp3 and wav. Cannot be used with reference_video_urls.

img_url.description: First frame image URL or Base64 encoded data. Required for I2V models. Image formats: JPEG, JPG, PNG, BMP, WEBP. Resolution: 360-2000 pixels. File size: max 10MB.

media.description:
Media asset list for wan2.7 and wan3.0 models. Specifies reference materials (image, audio, video)
for video generation. Each element contains a type and url field.
Supported type values vary by model:
- wan2.7-i2v: first_frame, last_frame, driving_audio, first_clip
- wan2.7-r2v: reference_image, reference_video
- wan2.7-videoedit: video, reference_image
- wan3.0-video: first_frame (max 1), last_frame (max 1), reference_image (max 10),
  reference_video (max 5 clips, total duration <= 15s), reference_audio (max 5 clips,
  total duration <= 15s), file (max 1, cannot be used with link), link (max 1, cannot
  be used with file). The reference_*/file/link types and first_frame/last_frame types
  are mutually exclusive within the same request. The array order defines the reference
  order of assets in the prompt (Image 1, Video 1, Audio 1, ...).

url.description: URL of the media file (public HTTP/HTTPS URL or OSS temporary URL)

negative_prompt.description: Reverse prompt words are used to describe content that you do not want to see in the video screen

prompt.description:
Text prompt words. Support Chinese and English, length not exceeding 800 characters
(up to 20,000 characters for wan3.0-video; content exceeding the limit is truncated).
For wan2.6-r2v with multiple reference videos, use 'character1', 'character2', etc. to refer to subjects
in the order of reference videos. Example: "Character1 sings on the roadside, Character2 dances beside it"
For wan3.0-video reference mode, use 'Image 1', 'Video 1', 'Audio 1', etc. to refer to media assets
in the corresponding order within the media array.

reference_video_urls.description:
Reference video URLs for wan2.6-r2v model only. Array of 1-3 video URLs.
Input restrictions:
- Format: mp4, mov
- Quantity: 1-3 videos
- Single video length: 2-30 seconds
- Single file size: max 30MB
- Cannot be used with audio_url
Reference duration: Single video max 5s, two videos max 2.5s each, three videos proportionally less.
Billing: Based on actual reference duration used.

template.description: Video effect template name. Optional. Currently supported: squish, flying, carousel. When used, prompt parameter is ignored.

model.description: The ID of the model to call. NOT constrained on this component: Comfy Router fills it from the `{model}` path segment of `POST /v2/models/wan/{model}`, so a Router caller omits it. A direct v1 call to `POST /proxy/wan/api/v1/services/aigc/video-generation/video-synthesis` MUST supply it, and the enum of accepted spellings lives on that operation's own component, `WanVideoGenerationRequest`.

audio.description: Whether to add audio to the video

audio_setting.description:
Video audio setting for wan2.7-videoedit model.
- auto (default): Model intelligently judges based on prompt content
- origin: Forcefully preserve the original audio from the input video

duration.description:
The duration of the video generated, in seconds:
- wan2.5 models: 5 or 10 seconds
- wan2.6-t2v, wan2.6-i2v: 5, 10, or 15 seconds
- wan2.6-r2v: 5 or 10 seconds only (no 15s support)
- wan2.7-i2v, wan2.7-t2v: integer in [2, 15]
- wan2.7-r2v, wan2.7-videoedit: integer in [2, 10]
- wan3.0-video: integer in [2, 30] without video input; with video input the total
  input video duration + output video duration must not exceed 30 seconds; -1 enables
  smart duration mode where the model picks a suitable duration

prompt_extend.description: Is it enabled prompt intelligent rewriting. Default is true

ratio.description:
Aspect ratio of the generated video. For wan2.7 and wan3.0 models only.
For wan2.7 models, defaults based on the resolution tier if not provided.
For wan3.0-video, adaptive (the default) automatically recommends a suitable
aspect ratio based on the input media proportions and intent.

resolution.description:
Resolution level. Supported values vary by model:
- wan2.5-i2v-preview: 480P, 720P, 1080P
- wan2.6-i2v: 720P, 1080P only (no 480P support)
- wan2.7 models (i2v, t2v, r2v, videoedit): 720P, 1080P (default 1080P)
- wan3.0-video, wan3.0-video-prime: 480P, 720P, 1080P (upstream default 1080P)
This proxy rejects video generation requests that provide neither resolution
nor size, because the resolution tier selects the billing rate.

seed.description: Random number seed, used to control the randomness of the model generated content

shot_type.description:
Intelligent multi-lens control. Only active when prompt_extend is enabled.
For wan2.6 and wan2.7-r2v models.
- single: Single-shot video (default)
- multi: Multi-shot video

watermark.description: Whether to add a watermark logo, the watermark is located in the lower right corner

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

code.description: Error code for a failed request, reported at the ROOT of the envelope rather than under `output` (not returned if the request succeeded).

message.description: Detailed information about a failed request, reported at the ROOT of the envelope rather than under `output` (not returned if the request succeeded). Read this before falling back to `output.message`.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Wan and HappyHorse models: the terminal `GET /proxy/wan/api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` document, forwarded unchanged. All three DashScope submit operations — `/api/v1/services/aigc/video-generation/video-synthesis` (video), `/api/v1/services/aigc/text2image/image-synthesis` (image) and `/api/v1/services/aigc/image2image/image-synthesis` (image) — are SUBMIT-AND-POLL: Router submits the task and then polls the one shared task-status route on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `{task_id, task_status}` handle the underlying submit answers with. That is the reading a modality-shaped guess gets backwards: unlike xAI and BytePlus, DashScope puts the IMAGE operations behind the same task queue as the video one, and all twenty ids answer this one document.
`output.task_status` is DashScope's own UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, `UNKNOWN` — forwarded unchanged. Router treats `SUCCEEDED` as the one terminal success for these models. `FAILED` and `CANCELED` are the terminal failures. `PENDING` and `RUNNING` are IN-FLIGHT and Router keeps polling on them, so a client must not abandon a task that reports either; `UNKNOWN` is treated as an unknown status and gets a bounded retry grace before it is failed.
WHICH LEAF CARRIES THE ASSET DEPENDS ON THE OPERATION, and a caller must select on the operation it submitted rather than on `output` being non-empty:
* VIDEO tasks (the eighteen video ids, submitted through
  `video-generation/video-synthesis`) put the generated video at
  `output.video_url`. An I2V task that also generated audio carries it separately at
  `output.check_audio`; that is not a substitute for `output.video_url`.
* IMAGE tasks (`wan/wan2.5-t2i-preview` through `text2image/image-synthesis` and
  `wan/wan2.5-i2i-preview` through `image2image/image-synthesis`) put each generated
  image at `output.results[].url`. `results` is a LIST — DashScope defaults to four
  images and honours `parameters.n` — and an individual element may carry `code` and
  `message` INSTEAD of `url` when that one image failed while the task as a whole
  succeeded, so a caller must read `url` per element rather than assume the list is
  uniform. `output.task_metrics` reports the TOTAL/SUCCEEDED/FAILED split for
  exactly that case.

A `SUCCEEDED` whose `output` carries neither leaf is a success that produced nothing, not a finished generation; through Router that distinction is already settled, because Router answers it as a Comfy Router error rather than with the provider document. A FAILED task reports its reason at `output.code`/`output.message`, and DashScope may additionally report a top-level `code`/`message` on the envelope itself; read the ROOT pair first and fall back to the nested one, which is the order the first-party Wan poller uses.
The URLs are DashScope-hosted and valid for 24 HOURS from completion, so download them promptly rather than storing them. `usage` reports DashScope's own generation accounting — its numbers, not the Comfy charge — and its fields are per-operation (`video_duration`/`video_ratio`/`video_count` for T2V, `duration`/`SR` for I2V and wan3.0-video, `size`/`image_count` for both image operations — T2I and I2I).
SCHEMA VS EXAMPLE: the schema below is the ONE shared `WanTaskQueryResponse` all twenty ids answer with — the wan/* output components are split only so that each published document carries an example of its OWN RESULT SHAPE, never a video example printed under an image model. The split is presentational; the contract is not.
THIS DOCUMENT describes a conditioned-video or wan3.0-video id, so its example is the video shape: the asset at `output.video_url` and the `duration`/`SR` usage pair.

output.actual_prompt: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water, slow motion, shallow depth of field
output.orig_prompt: a single red maple leaf falling onto still water

actual_prompt.description: Actual prompt after intelligent rewriting (for video tasks)

check_audio.description: Audio URL for I2V tasks with audio generation

code.description: The error code for the failed request (not returned if request is successful)

message.description: Detailed information about the failed request (not returned if request is successful)

results.description: List of task results for image generation tasks

actual_prompt.description: Actual prompt after intelligent rewriting (if enabled)

code.description: Image error code (returned when some tasks fail)

message.description: Image error information (returned when some tasks fail)

task_metrics.description: Task result statistics for image generation tasks

video_url.description: Video URL for completed video generation tasks. Link validity period 24 hours

usage.description: Output information statistics. Only successful results are counted

SR.description: Video resolution level (I2V and wan3.0-video tasks)

duration.description: Duration of generated video in seconds (I2V and wan3.0-video tasks)

fps.description: Frame rate of the generated video (wan3.0-video tasks)

image_count.description: Number of generated images (T2I and I2I tasks)

input_video_duration.description: Duration of the input video in seconds, 0.0 when no video input (wan3.0-video tasks)

output_video_duration.description: Duration of the output video in seconds (wan3.0-video tasks)

ratio.description: Aspect ratio of the generated video, e.g. 16:9 (wan3.0-video tasks)

video_duration.description: Duration of generated video in seconds (T2V tasks)
